terms.sense: An electrically neutral particle of an element with equal numbers of protons and electrons.
An atom or group of atoms with a net charge after gaining or losing electrons.
Atoms of the same element with the same proton number and different nucleon numbers.
A different structural form of the same element.
Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.
Attraction between the nuclei of bonded atoms and their shared electrons.
An amount of substance containing approximately 6.022 × 10²³ specified particles.
Approximately 6.022 × 10²³ particles per mole.
Average atomic mass relative to one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom; no unit.
Sum of the relative atomic masses in a chemical formula; no unit.
Mass or amount of dissolved substance per unit solution volume; specify g/dm³ or mol/dm³.
An acid that ionises completely in aqueous solution.
An acid that ionises only partially in aqueous solution.
A proton acceptor in the aqueous proton-transfer model used here.
A water-soluble base that gives hydroxide ions in aqueous solution.
An insoluble solid formed from substances in solution.
A homogeneous mixture of a solute and solvent.
A recorded change seen or measured, such as colour, a precipitate or gas bubbles.
A conclusion drawn from observations, such as the identity of a gas or ion.
Volume delivered from a burette, calculated as final reading minus initial reading.
Electrode at which oxidation occurs; positive in an electrolytic cell.
Electrode at which reduction occurs; negative in an electrolytic cell.
A molten or dissolved ionic substance that conducts through mobile ions.
Change in an appropriate measured quantity per unit time.
A substance that increases reaction rate and is chemically unchanged at the end.
In a closed system, forward and reverse reaction rates are equal and macroscopic composition remains constant.
Loss of electrons or gain of oxygen in the syllabus models.
Gain of electrons or loss of oxygen in the syllabus models.
Closeness of a measured value to the accepted value.
Closeness of repeated readings to one another, distinguished from accuracy.
The variable deliberately changed during an investigation.
The measured response in an investigation.
A relevant variable kept constant to make a fair comparison.
A compound containing carbon and hydrogen only.
A family sharing a functional group and general formula, with similar chemical properties.
A large molecule formed by joining repeating monomer units.
Capable of being broken down by microorganisms.
